subject: E-Commerce
title: The Blurring of Content and Commerce
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Blurring of Content and Commerce usable.

hook.text: Netflix tested shopping for outfits seen in shows. Amazon's ads in Freevee let you buy products mid-stream.

buildup.text: Shoppable content means every piece of media becomes a potential transaction point. See it, want it, buy it.

discovery.text: YouTube now lets creators tag products in videos. Viewers click and buy without leaving the video.

twist.text: The line between entertainment and advertisement is vanishing. When everything is shoppable, nothing is entertainment.

climax.text: The future is 'see it, buy it' everywhere: TV, social, gaming. Commerce becomes invisible, embedded in everything.

punchline.text: Buy the outfit from the show. When everything is shoppable, content IS commerce.

quiz.question: What does 'shoppable content' mean for the future?
options: Every piece of media becomes a potential purchase point
